mediumOfInstruction: Pre-primary targets English and French, scaffolded on the child's first language
The framework names that L1 only as the child's first language, never which one
Ombudsperson quotes Education Regulations s.43: in Standards IV to VI the medium is English
Up to and including Standard III any one language may be employed as the medium
The Minister decides which language that is, as most suitable for the pupils

sources.label: Mauritius Institute of Education, National Curriculum Framework Pre-Primary (2024), section 4.2 Communication, Language and Literacy

Ombudsperson for Children (Mauritius), 'Case 3: Kreol language in the education system', quoting Education Regulations s.43 'Medium of instruction and teaching of languages' — reproduced in full by LALIT; the Regulations themselves are not published on attorneygeneral.govmu.org or lawsofmauritius.govmu.org, and the Education Act carries no medium provision

mediumOfInstruction: Dual Immersion splits the school day equitably between Spanish and Portuguese
Each class has two teachers on the same official curriculum, one per language
It sits inside Ensenanza Primaria, in schools on the frontier
Began 2003 in three full-time schools in Artigas and Rivera, on the Brazil border
The programme now covers seven schools in three departments

sources.label: ANEP / DGEIP (Dirección General de Educación Inicial y Primaria), Programa de Inmersión Dual Español-Portugués — Departamento de Lenguas, Centro de Formación Permanente

mediumOfInstruction: Cuna Nahuat runs entirely in the indigenous language, used for all its activities
Early immersion from 2010 for children aged 3 to 5, at Santo Domingo de Guzman
A second cuna was founded in 2018 at Santa Catarina Masahuat, also in Sonsonate
It sits inside Universidad Don Bosco's Nahuat revitalisation project, begun 2003

sources.label: Universidad Don Bosco (El Salvador), 'El náhuat, última lengua indígena viva en El Salvador' — the university's own account of its Proyecto de Revitalización del Náhuat and of the Cuna Náhuat immersion programme it runs
Universidad Don Bosco, 'Cuna Náhuat: donde florece el náhuat', 10 December 2010 — close of the five-month pilot at Santo Domingo de Guzmán

revitalisation: Founding arrete sets the academy to fix definitively the rules of the Malagasy language
It published Rakibolana Miraki-pahalalana, 35,000 headwords over 1,133 pages
Akademia Malagasy, the national academy of arts, letters and sciences, does the work
Created by the arrete of 23 January 1902
The Academy issued the dictionary's first run in 2005

Akademia Malagasy, RAKIBOLANA RAKIPAHALALANA — the Academy's encyclopaedic Malagasy dictionary, first issued 2005
